alternatives.name: Dual MEMS piezoresistive sensors
alternatives.description: Two MEMS piezoresistive pressure sensors at shunt inlet (CSF) and outlet (venous), wired to an implanted ASIC that computes differential and runs occlusion prediction
alternatives.engineering_feasibility: HIGH — MEMS pressure sensors are FDA-cleared (CardioMEMS precedent)

alternatives.name: Single differential sensor across shunt body
alternatives.description: One pressure sensor spanning the shunt lumen, measuring differential directly rather than computing from two absolute measurements
alternatives.engineering_feasibility: MEDIUM — differential pressure sensors exist but integration across a shunt lumen is novel

alternatives.name: Optical fiber Bragg grating (FBG) pressure sensors
alternatives.description: Two FBG sensors at inlet/outlet, read via an external optical interrogator through a percutaneous fiber or wireless optical link
alternatives.engineering_feasibility: MEDIUM — FBG sensors are MRI-safe but require optical interrogator

alternatives.name: Capacitive pressure sensors with wireless readout
alternatives.description: Two capacitive pressure sensors with LC resonant circuit, read wirelessly by an external RFID-like reader
alternatives.engineering_feasibility: MEDIUM — wireless implantable pressure sensors exist (CardioMEMS) but dual-sensor differential is novel

alternatives.name: Hydrostatic column height differential
alternatives.description: A visible/imagable fluid column in a side branch whose height reflects the CSF-venous pressure differential, readable via ultrasound or X-ray
alternatives.engineering_feasibility: LOW — passive but not continuous; requires imaging to read

summary.strongest: ARCH-001 (dual MEMS piezoresistive) — highest feasibility, lowest cost, FDA-cleared precedent
